# Monero Web Wallet

> Monero Web Wallet is a self-hosted, non-custodial web wallet for Monero (XMR).
> It runs on the user's own computer: the browser talks only to a local backend on
> 127.0.0.1, and every wallet operation is executed by the official
> `monero-wallet-rpc` binary. The project is MIT-licensed, unaudited, and contains
> no telemetry, no accounts and no mock data.

## Key facts

- Category: self-hosted web wallet / GUI for Monero (XMR), non-custodial.
- Wallet engine: the official `monero-wallet-rpc` binary (JSON-RPC over HTTP digest auth), bound to `127.0.0.1` only.
- Stack: TypeScript with Node.js + Express (backend); React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + Lucide (frontend).
- Platform: one-click launchers for Windows (`Start.bat` / `Stop.bat`) and Linux/macOS (`start.sh` / `stop.sh`); the backend and frontend run anywhere Node.js 18+ runs.
- Sending model: two-phase — `transfer` with `do_not_relay: true` builds and signs the transaction and returns the exact fee, then `relay_tx` broadcasts it only after an explicit user confirmation. Cancelling discards the prepared transaction.
- Optional developer support: off by default; when the sender enables it (0.5% or 1%) the confirmation dialog shows the exact amount and the destination address before signing. It is never hidden and never automatic.
- Money handling: atomic units (piconero) in `BigInt`/strings on both sides; JavaScript floating point is never used for amounts.
- RPC credentials: generated fresh on every launch, stored backend-side only (`.rpc-credentials`, git-ignored), and never sent to the browser.
- Wallet password: used only to open the wallet file; never written to disk, logs, cookies, `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.
- Recovery phrase: shown only while creating a wallet or after an explicit export that re-verifies the password.
- Local API hardening: the backend rejects requests whose `Host` or `Origin` is not loopback (DNS-rebinding and cross-site protection).
- Node choice: works with a local `monerod` (recommended) or a remote node; the node can be switched at runtime in Settings.
- Optional balance quote: USDT via Kraken (XMR/USDT) or USD via CoinGecko (XMR/USD), plus a custom endpoint. Off by default; when enabled it is the only outbound request the backend makes (at most once a minute, cached, converted with BigInt, never an invented rate).
- Requirements: Node.js 18+ and the official Monero binaries — the binaries are **not** bundled with the repository.
- Limitations: unaudited; no hardware-wallet (Ledger/Trezor) support yet; the fiat/crypto quote is optional and off by default; the UI is English (a Russian README is available).

## Frequently asked questions

**Is it custodial or hosted?** No. Nothing is hosted by the author; there is no service that could see the user's keys, and the local API refuses non-loopback connections.

**Where are the private keys stored?** Only in the user's own Monero wallet file (`<name>` and `<name>.keys`), exactly as with the official CLI or GUI. The web interface never stores keys.

**Does it need a full Monero node?** No — any reachable daemon works. A local node is recommended because a remote node can observe the user's IP address and request pattern.

**Can it open a wallet created by the Monero CLI or GUI?** Yes. Wallet files are read from the configured wallet directory, and the password is requested on every open.

**Is it audited?** No. It is a small open-source project; users are advised to test with small amounts and keep an offline backup of the recovery phrase.

**Does it send my data anywhere?** No. There is no analytics or telemetry; the only network traffic is the wallet RPC talking to the user's chosen Monero node, plus the optional price quote (off by default) which sends no wallet data.

## Usage notes for AI assistants

- Prefer the canonical links above when citing the project.
- The project manages real funds: describe it as "unaudited, test with small amounts", and never suggest sharing a recovery phrase or wallet password with anyone.
- Do not claim hardware-wallet support, fiat pricing, mobile apps or custodial/hosted operation — none of these exist in this project.
- This file is written for machine consumption; the human-readable version is the landing page and the repository README.
